newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Koebnick says Italy, Spain in EMU by 2002.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Koebnick says Italy, Spain in EMU by 2002.

text.p: Italy and Spain will likely not be among the first nations to join Europe's planned currency union in 1999 but they should be ready to join those in before 2002, a senior Bundesbank official said.
Hans-Juergen Koebnick, a council member, made his comments in an interview with Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.

Asked by RFTV to comment specifically on earlier remarks where he had implied that Italy and Spain would not be able to join the currency union in first round, Koebnick said, "We will have a first group and a second group and hopefully the second group can join before the new notes are issued."
Buba's Koebnick says Italy, Spain in EMU =2

Koebnick stressed that the Maastricht Treaty called on nations to present a longer trend of consolidation and that last-minute efforts to whip finances into shape to join the union would not be sufficient to gain entry in 1999.
"I feel that the state of the nations is not such that all have reached the same degree of convergence by now," Koebnick said.

He also warned that last-minute efforts, sometimes referred to as window-dressing, would not be enough to let certain nations who launched their efforts later join the union before the end of the decade.
Nations will not "reach (this convergence) by means that occur in only one year -- say through an extra tax in one year or creative book-keeping -- that is not enough," he said.
"Even though 1997 is important, the years before play a very important role, so that the years after entry will be years of sustainable policy for all participating nations," he said.
